thread:
ara: Quick follow-up from the RFC — I'm proposing we shrink the private-endpoint operator handshake to a minimal, idempotent surface to simplify upgrades and reduce cross-account permissions.
sam: Can you sketch the minimal fields you'd keep? curious how this affects existing peering flows.
ara: Minimal idea: tenant_id, operator_token (short-lived), callback_url, and a capability bitmask. Everything else lives in config fetched after onboarding.
jin: That sounds reasonable. main tradeoff is extra roundtrips during cold start vs smaller IAM footprint. We should ensure the operator can resume with cached config.
maria: How do we handle cert rotation / KMS integration? if operator only gets a token, we need a way for us to push new cert metadata without re-onboarding.
ara: plan: token grants a control-plane channel scoped to tenant; we expose a cert-sync endpoint on the operator plane. rotation is a separate API call, no re-onboard needed.
devon: Rollout concern: not all customers will upgrade their operators at once. We need compatibility headers so old operators don't fail the new onboarding.
ara: agreed. propose versioned handshake: Accept v1 (current full payload) and v2 (minimal). server returns negotiated_version in response.
patrick: Observability requirements: expose metrics for handshake durations, failures by tenant, and a categorical reason (auth, config-mismatch, network). we must tie this to alerts.
ara: +1 on metrics. Also add a per-tenant last-success timestamp and optional debug log dump endpoint gated behind audit logs.
sam: Example API for v2? can you paste a tiny sample.
ara: sure:

```
POST /v2/operator/onboard
{
  "tenant_id": "t-1234",
  "operator_token": "ey...",
  "callback_url": "https://relay.ops.example/cb",
  "capabilities": ["egress", "metrics"]
}

200 OK
{
  "negotiated_version": "v2",
  "control_channel": "wss://cp.example/tenant/t-1234",
  "expires_at": "2026-04-01T12:00:00Z"
}
```

jin: If control_channel is a short lived websocket URL, operator can bootstrap and then use cached creds. Reconnect strategy needs jitter + exponential backoff.
maria: For KMS/HSM usage: operator shouldn't receive raw keys. we should issue ephemeral certs signed by our CA and let operator present those for mTLS to the control channel.
devon: Migration playbook idea: 1) support both v1 & v2 for 3 months, 2) opt-in migration flag for customers in console, 3) forced cutover after notice. any objections?
patrick: Auditability: all onboard and rotate calls must be logged to immutable audit store. also capture the negotiated_version and operator IP at time of onboarding.
ara: no objections. one more nuance: handling partial failures during a canary where the operator accepts v2 but the dataplane (in customer's VPC) still expects older behavior.
sam: fallback policy: if dataplane fails compatibility checks, server should return a compatibility_hint and a temporary feature-compat-mode header so operator can switch to compatibility fallback for X seconds.
jin: implement a feature flagging check at runtime. operator should be able to query /compat-check before switching traffic.
maria: security question: do we allow operators to request escalation (e.g., add egress capability) after onboarding? need RBAC and approval flow.
ara: require a signed request via operator's current token; escalation creates an audit entry and sets a pending flag. UI + API approve path for ops engineers.
devon: deployment: we'll feature-flag v2 behind a kill-switch. plan a staged rollout to dedicated clusters first, then hosted.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: staging rollout of operator-handshake-v2 started (canary group: 12 tenants) :rocket:
patrick: After canary, run a 72h stability window and check handshake error rate <0.1% and median handshake latency improvement >= 15%.
ara: ack — I'll draft the follow-up RFC summary with the migration playbook, compatibility headers, and metrics matrix. will ping infra and security for final review. :thumbsup:
